name: AI video
blurb: Make, generate, edit and deliver video: HyperFrames, video-model prompts, ffmpeg cuts, captions, beat cuts and QA.
searches: new text-to-video model release API pricing
image-to-video prompting technique camera control consistency
HyperFrames release new workflow or registry blocks
AI video editing agent transcript cut ffmpeg skill
auto captions talking head short-form editing technique

tests.prompt: I have a 9-minute talking-head recording (talk.mp4) with lots of ums and two false starts. Make a 60-second vertical clip for Reels with captions. Tell me exactly what you will run and in what order.
tests.good: Probes and transcribes word-level first; proposes a cut strategy and waits for approval; cuts on word boundaries with 30-200 ms padding and 30 ms fades; reframes 9:16 before burning captions; captions last, at most 2 lines, inside the Reels safe zone; loudness -14 LUFS with true peak at or below -1 dBTP; verifies with a probe and a contact sheet.

tests.prompt: Write the prompts and settings to turn our product photo (bottle.png) into three 5-second b-roll clips for a 9:16 ad, and pick a model. The brand name must be perfectly readable.
tests.good: Uses image-to-video from the photo; one camera move per clip, varied across clips; describes motion and what stays still; keeps the brand name out of the generated layer (code overlay) or protects the label; states model, cost and number of takes before generating; credentials from environment variables only.

tests.prompt: Turn this 900-word blog post about compound interest into a 60-second narrated explainer for YouTube Shorts. Give me the plan you would get approved first.
tests.good: States a one-sentence message and 1080x1920 aspect; picks one explainer structure and does not follow paragraph order; hook in the first 3 s with the thesis by beat 2; 10-12 beats with timings that add up to about 60 s and about 140 voiceover words; on-screen numbers set in code; captions from word timings; asks for approval before rendering.

tests.prompt: Make a 45-second TikTok teaser for our note-taking app: a few AI b-roll shots of the same person sketching ideas in a cafe, a real screen recording of the app, a voiceover and a music bed, with captions. Plan the shots before generating anything.
tests.good: States a short plan first: shots through storyboarding (shot-lists-and-boards.md, keyframes-and-consistency.md: one identity string so the person stays the same), voiceover and bed through audio-generation (voiceover-tts.md, music-generation.md: about 100 words of VO, one voice, instrumental bed), then here: hybrid route (plan-and-route.md), b-roll prompts (generative-prompting.md), screen recording and assembly (explainers-and-promos.md), delivery (delivery-qa.md). Hook in 3 s; app name and UI text in code; model and cost stated before paid takes; captions last inside the TikTok safe zone; -14 LUFS; checks the Done means of all three crafts.

tests.prompt: I recorded a 40-minute founder interview on two cameras (A: wide, B: close-up, separate audio recorder). My editor finishes everything in Premiere Pro. Do the rough cut for me: drop the ums and false starts, keep the three strongest stories, about 6 minutes total, and hand it to her as something she can open in Premiere and keep editing, not just a flattened MP4. Also give me a 9:16 Reels cut of the best 45 seconds. We have the Adobe connector in Claude if that helps.
tests.good: Delivers the rough cut as an editable Premiere timeline: either an interchange file Premiere imports (FCP7 XML or EDL/AAF) that references the original camera and audio files at their real paths with matching frame rate and timecode, or a sequence built in desktop Premiere through its UXP scripting or a local MCP bridge, saying which and noting that the third-party bridge has telemetry on by default; scopes the Adobe for creativity connector correctly: its video tools (video_create_quick_cut, video_render, video_resize) work on uploaded cloud copies, not on her Premiere project, and Quick Cut picks moments by relevance rather than exact transcript cuts, so it is at most used for the Reels draft and uploading the interview is asked first; cuts from a word-level transcript on word boundaries with padded edges and keeps the EDL as the source of truth; syncs camera A, camera B and the external recorder (timecode or audio waveform) and keeps the angles on separate tracks or as a multicam source instead of assuming they line up; makes the 9:16 version with the face kept inside the vertical safe zone (Premiere's Auto Reframe or a tracked crop) and supplies captions as an SRT for a Premiere caption track rather than burned in, since the editor will refine; verifies before handing over (the XML or EDL parses, sequence length matches the EDL total, a contact sheet of the Reels cut) and lists anything the editor must relink; leaves the camera originals untouched and writes outputs to new paths.

tools.name: FFmpeg
tools.why: The universal engine under nearly every editor, converter and agent video workflow; the ffmpeg skill (kajisho5) has 1.6k stars and the AI editors in this list all shell out to it.

tools.name: HyperFrames
tools.why: HeyGen's open-source HTML-to-video framework built for agents: 56.7k GitHub stars, Apache-2.0, ships 20+ first-party skills (agent-first framing in the vibeknow and pexo comparisons).

tools.name: Remotion
tools.why: The incumbent React framework for programmatic video: 61.8k GitHub stars, official agent skills launched Jan 2026 and reported at 150k installs on skills.sh (gaga.art/ngram write-ups); company licence needed for teams of 4+.

tools.name: Google Veo 3.1 / Gemini Omni (Gemini API)
tools.why: Top-ranked in 2026 round-ups for physical realism and native-audio dialogue (mstudio, tech-insider, teamday); Google's docs now recommend Gemini Omni Flash as the default and Veo 3.1 for extension and last-frame control.

tools.name: Kling AI
tools.why: One of the four best-in-class 2026 models (Runway, Veo, Kling, Seedance) per mstudio and getaiperks round-ups; Kling 3.0 holds several AA top-10 entries and about $0.10 per second.

tools.name: Runway
tools.why: Named with Veo, Kling and Seedance as best-in-class for creative control in the mstudio and teamday round-ups; its API now also hosts Seedance 2.5, Gen-4.5 and Aleph 2.0 video-to-video.

tools.name: Seedance (ByteDance ModelArk / BytePlus)
tools.why: Picked as the commercial and product-content leader in 2026 round-ups (mstudio, seeddance) and available first-party and through Runway, fal and others.

tools.name: HeyGen (Video Agent, avatars)
tools.why: Default AI-presenter service; HeyGen's own docs ship an MCP server, CLI and llms.txt, and it publishes skills for video, avatar and translate. Promoted to major by the critic: HeyGen and Synthesia are the two named leaders for AI avatar video in 2026 round-ups (rework, synthesia), and HeyGen also maintains HyperFrames.

tools.name: fal.ai (genmedia CLI)
tools.why: Aggregator with 1,000+ model endpoints (Kling, Veo, Seedance, LTX, Wan) behind one API and CLI; the usual way agents reach several video models with one key.

tools.name: Luma Dream Machine (Ray)
tools.why: Established text/image-to-video API with official Python and JS SDKs; appears in 2026 skill prompt lists next to Runway and Pika but not in the top four.

tools.name: DaVinci Resolve
tools.why: About 15% of the pro desktop editing market and in 4 of 5 profiled creator stacks (Storyblocks survey, via sendshort and chatcut round-ups); Studio 21.1 ships a native Blackmagic MCP server (File > Setup AI Assistants) built on its Python scripting API.

tools.name: CapCut
tools.why: Most-used video editing app overall (800M+ monthly users, about 81% of mobile editing per sendshort); no official public API, so agents work on its local draft JSON files. Promoted to major by the critic: CapCut passed 1 billion downloads and holds about 81% of mobile editing (sendshort 2026), so most short-form creators finish there even without an API.

tools.name: Adobe Premiere Pro (and the Adobe for creativity connector)
tools.why: Largest desktop pro editor, about 35% of the desktop pro market ahead of Final Cut (25%) and Resolve (15%) (sendshort 2026 statistics); default for agencies and newsrooms. Adobe's official 'Adobe for creativity' Claude connector (Apr 2026, expanded Sep 2026) lists Premiere among its 80+ tools; its public skills (adobe/skills) call cloud video tools video_resize, video_create_quick_cut and video_render on uploaded assets, not on a local .prproj. Desktop Premiere is scriptable through the UXP DOM API (sequences, tracks, clips, markers, project items) and imports FCP7 XML, EDL and AAF.

tools.name: Final Cut Pro (FCPXML)
tools.why: About 25% of the desktop pro editing market, second to Premiere (sendshort 2026), and the standard for Mac-based productions. No official API or connector; automation is FCPXML import/export (libraries, events, projects, spine, asset-clips, markers, roles) plus AppleScript and Compressor, which community MCP servers build on.

tools.name: Descript
tools.why: Leading text-based (transcript) editor for talking-head, podcast and screen-recording video; named with OpusClip and Captions as the leaders for turning long recordings into captioned clips in 2026 round-ups. Has an official Claude connector (May 2026, first-party hosted MCP at api.descript.com/v2/mcp with OAuth) and a REST API: import with transcription, Underlord edits (fillers, Studio Sound, captions, highlight reels), transcript export incl. SRT, publish links; imports use media minutes and edits use AI credits.

tools.name: Synthesia
tools.why: With HeyGen, the AI-avatar market leader; dominant for corporate training and internal comms (vendor says used by 90%+ of the Fortune 100; 55K+ companies in 2025; $4B valuation Jan 2026). Video API for scripted avatar videos, templates, dubbing and translation (async jobs), Upload API, Interactive Avatars API.

tools.name: OpusClip
tools.why: Best-known long-to-short repurposing tool (auto clip selection, branded captions, reframe to any aspect); listed with Descript and Captions as leaders for turning long recordings into short captioned clips. Self-serve API with bearer token, official SDKs and an MCP server for agents.

tools.name: Avid Media Composer
tools.why: Still cuts more feature films and broadcast shows than any other NLE thanks to shared-storage workflows, but its footprint outside those sectors is small (thepostflow, editorskeys 2026). Interchange is AAF and EDL, with OTIO import since 2025.6; relevant when an AI rough cut must hand off to a broadcast or film editor. Docs page returned 403 to the fetcher.
